newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bond prices closed lower in moderate trade on Thursday in line with a hike in the interbank rate, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked down across the board following a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.08/2.03 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 2.00/1.95 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.63/1.58 percent against 1.57/1.52 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.26/99.31 from Wednesday's close of S$99.32/99.37, September 2001 at S$99.27/99.32 versus S$99.36/99.41 and June 2003 at S$98.81/98.86 against S$98.93/98.98.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-7/16 3-5/16 percent from Wednesday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
